newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ABB shares dip on board shuffle.
newsitem.headline: ABB shares dip on board shuffle.

text.p: Shares in ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG eased in pre-bourse trading on the Swiss Exchange after the electrical engineering group announced that Goeran Lindahl would take over the functions of president and chief executive from Percy Barnevik, who remains chairman.

Dealers said the fall in ABB's shares was initially triggered by worries that Barnevik would relinquish all his functions in ABB, a company that embodies his vision of a global engineering group that acts in an accordance to the principles of sustained development.

Since the merger of Sweden's ASEA AB and Swiss BBC Brown Boveri AG in 1988 into ABB, Barnevik's vision has dominated the company, which has aggresively expanded into Eastern Europe and Asia, while reducing its workforce in Europe.
Bearer shares in ABB were down nine Swiss francs, or 0.58 percent, on the Swiss Exchange to 1,547 Swiss francs, the largest loser in generally weak pre-bourse trade.
ABB will report nine month results on October 22 and a spokesman said the company is sticking to this schedule.
